findings.reason: without a followup naming s42, s43 and s44 the plan's newest implementable work enters no build invocation and the fixes it authors are never queued.
findings.text: f-qwnw-006, the plan's only open followup, states "Sections 3, 29, 33, 35, 36 and 41 are the plan's remaining implementable work" and queues `/reckon-build queued-work-needs-no-workaround §3 §29 §33 §35 §36 §41`, while the section declarations at line 23 of the same document now read s3, s29, s33 and s35 as done and declare the three new sections s42, s43 and s44 implementable, so no followup, decision or dependency names the three sections this change adds and a dispatcher following the prompt rebuilds four landed sections while never dispatching s42, s43 or s44

findings.reason: the gate would certify a fix that leaves the surface the incident was actually reported from unchanged, so the node closes with the fault still live there.
findings.text: s43's endpoint covers "A dispatch, resume or review refused at the scratch floor", and the incident it cites was observed through a `crew resume` ("Review dispatches and a `crew resume` were refused with `tmp-headroom-refusal`"), but the gate asserts only that "A refused dispatch's JSON names each owner with its bytes and session", so a fix that enriches the dispatch refusal while the resume and review refusals keep naming free bytes and the floor alone passes every stated assertion

findings.reason: the unmeasured half is the half that keeps a lane's dead login from being read as the node's own failure, so the gate can pass while the false outcome the section exists to stop survives.
findings.text: s44's endpoint requires that an authentication-refused launch "is recorded as `launch-failed` with a failure kind naming the lane's login and the refusal text, and it does not count as the node's outcome", but the done-when's first bullet asserts only the refusal kind and text; nothing in the gate observes how the run is counted, and at the base revision a `launch-failed` phase is already bucketed with `failed` where a project view counts run phases (reckon/crew/runs.py:4140-4141), so a fix that renames the failure and leaves the run counted as a node failure passes every stated assertion

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every existing module a write path names resolves in the tree (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py, reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py, reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py, reckon/_backends.py, reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, reckon/crew/station.py, reckon/crew/ticker.py); scratch_headroom_watch.py and lane_login_watch.py are named as new modules in the existing `*_watch.py` family beside dispatch_watch.py, gate_watch.py, lift_watch.py and recovery_watch.py, as the new test files and the sNN.html fragments are deliverables that cannot resolve yet; and the cited plan resolves at docs/plans/delivered-work-lands-without-a-coordinator.html.
rubric_items.done_when: two findings — s43's gate drives only a refused dispatch while the fault it cites arrived through a refused `crew resume`, and s44's gate never measures the "does not count as the node's outcome" half of its endpoint sentence.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — each section's evidence fragment writes under docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/, a durable path inside the repository.
rubric_items.naming: pass — section titles, test file names and prose describe the mechanism (a landing leaving its base trees, a scratch floor announced with its owners, a dead lane login) with no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each section's stated cause matches the evidence it cites (s42's unheld landing-base-* trees, created through reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:1651-1696 under the reckon-crew-scratch root; s43's bare tmp-headroom-refusal raised at reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:905-908; s44's picker reading gate outcomes and quota while reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py carries no login notion), each endpoint is obtainable from that system and falsifiable by its stated negative control, and none of the three prescribes a code path, step sequence, formula or function to call.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of s42, s43 and s44 names one fault with one remedy: a scratch tree outliving its landing, a scratch refusal that names no owner, and a lane whose login is dead.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the only open followup f-qwnw-006 (docs/plans/queued-work-needs-no-workaround.html:445) names five sections the document now declares done and omits the three sections this change adds, so s42, s43 and s44 are carried by no build invocation.
